newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks outlook bright after Fed - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks outlook bright after Fed - analysts.

text.p: Bright fundamentals could lift Mexican stocks out of the doldrums after U.S. Federal Reserve policy makers meet on September 24, even if official U.S. interest rates rise as expected, analysts said on Friday.
Volume on the Mexican stock market has averaged at a thin 62 million shares per session over the last two weeks.

"In general, any increase in U.S. rates would affect us because it would stem foreign investment inflow and Mexican exports to the U.S., and would hamper debt or equity placements," said Esteban Rojas, deputy director of research at the Akra brokerage.

"However, we feel that rate hikes would have a short-lived effect, as investors are looking ahead to domestic factors, like the Alliance for Economic Recovery (a pact between the government, business and labor), forthcoming third quarter results, and good prospects for next year," Rojas added.
The Fed's Federal Open Market Committee meeting is widely expected to result in a hike of 25 basis points in official U.S. interest rates.
Mexican markets have already discounted that likelihood, and such a move could even beneficial by sweeping away a cloud of uncertainty, analysts said.

"If (U.S.) rates go up 25 basis points, that's already been discounted, and once it happens, it'll get rid of uncertainty and that would improve market activity," said Carlos Smano, reserch director at the Bancomer brokerage.
"Too much attention has been paid to external factors, when there really has been much progress on the domestic political and economic fronts," Smano said.
If U.S. rate hikes were to bring the leading IPC index down to supports at 3,270 or 3,250 points, then Mexican stocks would be a great buy opportunity among emerging markets.
"We would be first or second preference among emerging markets, now Argentina and Brazil are having financial problems," said another equity analyst.
"With cheap prices and medium-term growth possibilities, I don't see why we shouldn't be a destination for speculative capital," he added.

At the close of trade on September 19, the IPC had gained 23.65 percent for the year to date in dollar terms, compared to 6.4 percent and 45.6 percent for the Argentine Merval and Brazilian Bovespa indices, respectively.
Analaysts also said that an uptrend in local interest rates could benefit stocks, as higher rates would weaken the peso, and thus make stocks cheaper for foreign buyers.

"We think that rates cannot go down any further due to the seasonal inflationary bubble during the months ahead, but that would lead to a more attractive exchange rate for foreign investors," said a trader from Santander brokerage.
